alignments.note: Rule 70: the ASV writes no word for the correlative μέν, and marking the correlation elsewhere is not writing it.
Rule 65's English-side test: the ASV writes no word for the adjunctive καί.
Participle recast as a noun phrase with a supplied preposition; the head is the nominal word, discontinuous under rule 15.

The verb's whole English frame preached he good tidings unto; rule 66 heads on tidings, the corpus spending preach on κηρύσσω (see s008 of 3.3) and good tidings on the εὐαγγελ- lexeme. Rule 106's accusative arm keeps unto inside the verb's unit rather than on the object. Heading on preached remains defensible.

review_notes: unto is kept with the verb under rule 106's accusative arm, an accusative having no case for an English preposition to realize; giving unto the to the article under rule 21 is the competing reading.
